Use a retrieval system that stores or filters documents by temporal validity, and make the model use that date information when deciding whether evidence still applies [1, 4, 8]. Chronofy embeds temporal validity into representation, retrieval, and reasoning, NuggetIndex keeps a validity interval and filters deprecated nuggets before ranking, and the recency taxonomy in RecencyQA helps determine when a question actually needs up-to-date information [4, 8, 3].

If you want a practical retrieval layer, a recency-aware hybrid reranker can reduce stale-document poisoning when dates are accurate, and news retrieval can be improved by time-localized selection over a dynamic structure [1, 7]. The papers also warn that date filters alone can be unreliable because retrieval may still leak post-cutoff information, so you need stronger safeguards than simple date filtering [2].
